# Health Communication

## Communicate so that information can be understood, trusted and used.

This applied course connects communication theory to real public-health decisions. Learners move from communication fundamentals and behavioural theory through audience insight, clinical communication, community engagement, message design, media strategy, digital communication, risk communication, infodemic management, evaluation and ethics.

<span class="lipps-chip">12 weeks</span> <span class="lipps-chip">Applied cases</span> <span class="lipps-chip">Timed objective quizzes</span> <span class="lipps-chip">Moodle-ready</span>
:::

::: {.lipps-section}
## Course philosophy

LIPPS Health Communication is built around one principle:

> **Communication succeeds only when the intended audience can access it, interpret it, trust it and use it in a real decision.**

The course therefore treats communication as a public-health intervention that must be diagnosed, designed, implemented and evaluated—not as the production of posters or social-media content.
:::

::: {.lipps-section}
## By the end of the course, learners should be able to

- diagnose health communication problems before selecting messages or channels;
- use behavioural and communication theory to explain determinants of action;
- analyse audiences, culture, health literacy, accessibility and communication environments;
- conduct effective interpersonal and clinical communication;
- design participatory community engagement and feedback systems;
- develop and pre-test clear, actionable messages;
- select integrated channel and media strategies;
- design safer, more equitable digital health communication;
- communicate uncertainty and risk during public-health emergencies;
- identify and manage misinformation, disinformation and infodemic problems;
- design and evaluate health communication campaigns; and
- apply ethical, equity and AI-governance principles to health communication.
:::

::: {.lipps-section}
## The 12-week course

<div class="lipps-week-grid">

<div class="lipps-week"><span>01</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-01.qmd">Foundations of Health Communication</a></h3><p>Explain health communication as a strategic public-health process that connects evidence, audiences, messages, channels, feedback and action.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>02</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-02.qmd">Communication and Behaviour-Change Theory</a></h3><p>Use behavioural and communication theory to diagnose why a health behaviour occurs and to select plausible communication and non-communication responses.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>03</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-03.qmd">Audience Analysis, Culture and Health Literacy</a></h3><p>Use formative audience insight, health-literacy principles and cultural context to design communication that people can access, understand and use.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>04</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-04.qmd">Interpersonal and Clinical Communication</a></h3><p>Use patient-centred interpersonal communication to elicit concerns, explain information clearly, check understanding and support informed decisions.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>05</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-05.qmd">Community Engagement and Participatory Communication</a></h3><p>Design community engagement as a two-way, accountable process that shares information, listens, adapts interventions and builds workable solutions with affected communities.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>06</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-06.qmd">Message Development and Pre-testing</a></h3><p>Develop clear, actionable health messages from defined objectives and improve them through systematic pre-testing with intended audiences.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>07</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-07.qmd">Communication Channels and Media Strategy</a></h3><p>Select and combine communication channels and messengers according to audience access, trust, objective, reach, frequency, interactivity, cost and decision timing.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>08</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-08.qmd">Digital Health and Social Media Communication</a></h3><p>Design and evaluate digital health communication while accounting for platform dynamics, privacy, accessibility, digital exclusion and the difference between engagement metrics and health outcomes.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>09</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-09.qmd">Risk and Crisis Communication</a></h3><p>Communicate rapidly and transparently during health threats while acknowledging uncertainty, supporting protective action, listening to affected communities and adapting as evidence changes.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>10</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-10.qmd">Misinformation, Disinformation and Infodemic Management</a></h3><p>Identify harmful information problems, prioritise them by likely health impact and respond through listening, accurate communication, trusted messengers, community engagement and resilience-building.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>11</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-11.qmd">Communication Campaign Design and Evaluation</a></h3><p>Design a coherent health communication campaign from problem diagnosis through objectives, strategy, implementation, monitoring and evaluation.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

<div class="lipps-week"><span>12</span><div><h3><a href="health-communication/week-12.qmd">Ethics, Equity and the Future of Health Communication</a></h3><p>Evaluate health communication for ethical integrity, equity, accessibility and responsible use of emerging technologies, then integrate the full course using the LIPPS SIGNAL framework.</p><strong>Mastery:</strong> 10 timed scenario questions sampled from a curated 30-item bank.</div></div>

</div>

::: {.lipps-section}
## How every week works

**ORIENT** — begin with a realistic public-health communication problem.  
**LEARN** — build concepts and decision frameworks.  
**APPLY** — work through an integrated case.  
**PRACTISE** — answer untimed reasoning questions with feedback in Moodle.  
**DEMONSTRATE** — complete a short timed mastery quiz drawn from a larger question bank.

The weekly quizzes are designed to be **AI-resilient rather than “AI-proof.”** Scenario-based items, random banks, shuffled options and calibrated time limits make knowing the material the most efficient strategy while preserving normal accessibility and approved accommodations.

[Read the LIPPS assessment model →](assessment-model.qmd)
:::

::: {.lipps-section}
## Source backbone

The course draws on established health-communication and behavioural-science literature, with particular emphasis on the **WHO Strategic Communications Framework**, **WHO Risk Communication and Community Engagement guidance and competency framework**, **WHO infodemic-management resources**, behavioural theories commonly used in health promotion, and programme-planning principles from *Making Health Communication Programs Work*.

LIPPS adds original instructional syntheses, African public-health scenarios, structured decision problems and the **LIPPS SIGNAL** capstone framework.

[Open the core reading list →](health-communication/core-readings.qmd)
:::

::: {.lipps-section}
## Core readings and pilot status

The course is suitable for a **university teaching pilot**, but the current Moodle banks should not yet be used as a high-stakes examination bank. Many foundation items are useful for practice; mastery items must be separated, rewritten toward novel scenarios and then piloted.

[Core readings →](health-communication/core-readings.qmd)  
[University pilot assessment blueprint →](pilot-assessment-blueprints.qmd)
:::

::: {.lipps-section}
## Course access

The public syllabus remains open. Lessons, quizzes, grades and learner progress are designed for **LIPPS Learn on Moodle**. Until the Moodle instance is connected, these pages serve as the **core lesson source and public preview**. For a university pilot, weekly lessons should be paired with the assigned readings, facilitated activities and authentic assessments described in the pilot blueprint.
:::
